# Malika Kishwar

Malika Kishwar Bahadur Fakr-ul-Zamani Nawab Taj Ara Begum (1803–1858), also known as Jenab Aliya Begum, was Queen Mother of the last King of Awadh. The wife of the tenth King of Awadh, Amjad Ali Shah, her son Nawab Wajid Ali Shah succeeded his father when she was widowed in 1847. After her son was placed under arrest for refusing to sign the annexation treaty, she met with British authorities in Lucknow to plead their case. In 1856, Queen Malika travelled to England and met with Queen Victoria in 1857. After the intervention of France, she was given permission to travel to Mecca on her way home, but died the next day. She is buried in a grave at Père Lachaise Cemetery in Paris.
Early life and marriage
Malika Kishwar Taj Ara Begum was born in 1803. She was from the Delhi-based family of Mughal court poet and minister Abdul Rahim Khan-i-Khanan.
